questions.question: Q1. Find the dimensions of [a/b²] in the Van der Waals equation:  (P + a/V²)(V − b) = nRT
questions.solution: In the Van der Waals equation, the term a/V² must have dimensions of Pressure = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]. Volume V has dimensions [L³]. So [a] = [P][V²] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²][L⁶] = [M L⁵ T⁻²]. Also [b] = [V] = [L³]. Therefore [a/b²] = [M L⁵ T⁻²] / [L⁶] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²].
questions.source: [JEE Main  |  27 Jan 2024  |  Evening Shift  |  Memory Based]

questions.question: Q2. Find the value of P in the dimensional equation:  M¹ = [Cᴺ G⁻½ h¹ᐟ²] Where: •  C = Speed of light  [L T⁻¹] •  G = Universal gravitational constant  [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²] •  h = Planck's constant  [M L² T⁻¹]
questions.solution: Dimensional analysis: [Cᴺ G⁻½ h¹ᐟ²] = [L T⁻¹]ᴺ [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²]⁻½ [M L² T⁻¹]¹ᐟ². Collect powers of M: 0·P + (½) + (½) = 1. This gives P(0) + 1 = 1 for M. Solving carefully, comparing M exponents: (1/2) from G⁻¹ᐟ² and (1/2) from h¹ᐟ² gives M¹. For consistency with L and T, P = 1/2.
questions.source: [JEE Main  |  30 Jan 2024  |  Evening Shift  |  Memory Based]

questions.question: Q3. Match the physical quantities with their correct dimensional formulae: (1)  P−1, Q−2, R−3, S−4 (2)  P−4, Q−3, R−2, S−1 (3)  P−1, Q−3, R−4, S−2 (4)  P−4, Q−2, R−1, S−3
questions.solution: Surface tension S = F/L  ⇒  [M T⁻²]. Viscosity η = F/(A · dv/dx)  ⇒  [M L⁻¹ T⁻¹]. Angular momentum L = r × p  ⇒  [M L² T⁻¹]. Rotational KE = ½Iω²  ⇒  [M L² T⁻²].

questions.question: Q4. Consider the two statements about dimensions: Statement-1: Angular momentum and Planck's constant have the same dimensions. Statement-2: Moment of force (torque) and linear momentum have the same dimensions. (1)  Both statements are true (2)  Both statements are false (3)  Statement 1 is true and Statement 2 is false (4)  Statement 2 is true and Statement 1 is false
questions.answer: (3)  Statement 1 is true; Statement 2 is false
questions.solution: Angular momentum [L] = r × p = [M L² T⁻¹]. Planck's constant [h] = E/ν = [M L² T⁻¹]. Both are equal — Statement 1 is TRUE. Torque [τ] = r × F = [M L² T⁻²], but Linear momentum [p] = mv = [M L T⁻¹]. These are NOT equal — Statement 2 is FALSE.

questions.question: Q5. Match Maxwell's equations to their correct names/laws:
options: (a)  A → Q, B → S, C → R, D → P
(b)  A → S, B → S, C → P, D → R
(c)  A → S, B → Q, C → R, D → P
(d)  A → Q, B → P, C → S, D → R
questions.solution: A: ∮B⃗·dA⃗=0 → Gauss law of magnetism (no magnetic monopoles). B: ∮E⃗·dA⃗=Q/ε₀ → Gauss law of electrostatics. C: ∮B⃗·dl⃗=μ₀i → Ampere's law. D: ∮E⃗·dl⃗=−dΦ_B/dt → Faraday & Lenz's law. Compiled by Saarathi  ·  JEE Main 2024 Physics  ·  Units & Dimensions PYQ Bank
